sources.entry: TocaPad - Slide your trackpad's edges to change volume and brightness, and double-tap a corner to run a shortcut. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/getguruhat/tocapad-macos) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: TocaPad is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that changes volume and brightness by sliding a finger along the edges of the trackpad, with optional double-tap corner shortcuts.
summary.what_it_does: TocaPad lets you slide one finger up or down the right edge of the trackpad to change volume, or the left edge to change brightness, with a level indicator shown at the top right of the screen. The edges are configurable: each control can be set to the left, right, top or bottom edge, or turned off. Double-tapping a trackpad corner can mute, play or pause, skip a track, open Mission Control, show the desktop, lock the screen, take a screenshot, open an app, or send a recorded keyboard shortcut; these corner actions are off by default. Settings include an ignore-while-typing option, cursor freeze during slides, fine steps with Shift-Option, sensitivity and edge width sliders, and Open at login. The menu has Levels, Edges, Corners and General tabs, and the menu bar icon can be hidden. The README says the app checks GitHub once a day for a new release and has no analytics.
use_cases: adjust Mac volume by sliding the trackpad edge
change display brightness without keyboard keys
map a double-tap trackpad corner to a shortcut
mute or pause media from a trackpad corner
lock screen or take screenshot with a trackpad tap
avoid accidental volume changes while typing
notable: Slide-to-adjust volume and brightness on trackpad edges with one finger; a second finger cancels so scrolling still works
Ignore-while-typing option stops resting palms from changing volume
Configurable edges and optional bottom-quarter-only response
Double-tap corner actions, including recorded keyboard shortcuts, with an option for tap-to-click double-click
Free, MIT-licensed, with no account or analytics
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon (M1 and newer), per the README download section
Brightness only works on the built-in display and Apple displays; most other monitors show 'Not adjustable'
Relies on undocumented macOS frameworks (MultitouchSupport, DisplayServices), so a macOS update could break it
App is not notarized by Apple, so the first launch must be allowed in System Settings > Privacy & Security
Keyboard-shortcut and media-key corner actions require Accessibility permission
